Title: Floods forecast in nine Kelantan districts until Wednesday
Article:
KOTA BARU: Nine districts in Kelantan are expected to experience flooding from today until Wednesday, following a continuous rain warning issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
The National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre of the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) said the districts are Kota Baru, Tumpat, Bachok, Machang, Pasir Mas, Pasir Puteh, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Jeli.
It said the preliminary flood forecast was issued following a Continuous Rain Warning (Alert) by MetMalaysia at 4.30pm today, with flood hotspots, low-lying areas and other flood-prone locations expected to be affected.
"In Kota Baru, areas at risk are located within the Kelantan River Basin, while in Tumpat, they are within the Golok River Basin, covering Sungai Golok, Sungai Pengkalan Nangka, Sungai Mentua and Sungai Kelaboran," it said in a statement.
In Bachok, areas at risk are within the Kemasin River Basin, including Sungai Jelawat, Sungai Kemasin, Saliran PKS, Saliran KADA and Sungai Bator.
The Semerak River Basin, covering Sungai Lubuk Nibong, Sungai Melor, Sungai Gunong and Sungai Semerak, is also at risk of flooding.
In Machang, areas at risk are within the Kelantan River Basin, including Sungai Kelantan, Sungai Kerawang, Sungai Kweng Hitam and watercourses in Machang town.
In Pasir Mas, flooding is forecast in the Golok River Basin, including Sungai Golok and Sungai Lemal, while areas at risk in Pasir Puteh are within the Semerak River Basin.
In Tanah Merah, areas at risk are within the Kelantan River Basin.
In Kuala Krai, the areas at risk include Sungai Lebir and Sungai Galas, both part of the Kelantan River Basin.
In Jeli, the areas at risk are Sungai Pergau and Sungai Jeli within the Kelantan River Basin, as well as Sungai Lanas in the Golok River Basin.
The department cautioned that flooding could occur earlier or later than forecast.
Residents, particularly those in flood-prone areas, are advised to remain vigilant and comply with instructions from the authorities.
The public can obtain the latest flood updates through the Public InfoBanjir website at https://publicinfobanjir.water.gov.my/.

Title: NST Leader: Don't let Malaysia's connectivity be a gateway for drugs
Article:
SITTING astride the Strait of Malacca in the centre of Southeast Asia has brought the country immense blessings, from being a shipping hub since time immemorial to being an essential aviation centre for regional and international airlines in more recent times.
With this has come trade and tourism, making Malaysia a strategic magnet for people from all over. With blessings, though, usually comes a potential curse; that we attract also less savoury characters and those who have a criminal bent.
We need, therefore, not just to reap the clear economic advantages of our strategic location but also to take care that it does not become a strategic weakness. The same connectivity that makes the country a regional trade, aviation and logistics hub also provides opportunities for drug traffickers to move their illicit cargo across borders.
This being the case, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail let on that the cabinet has approved a joint memorandum between the home and transport ministries on Aug 19 for the implementation of a comprehensive, short to medium and long-term action plan on Security Improvement and Mitigation to strengthen phased-in security controls and screening at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and other international entry points.
Malaysia's proximity to the Golden Triangle, one of the world's major drug-producing regions, puts it in a particularly vulnerable position. This is not merely a theoretical concern.
In March, police seized more than 3.4 tonnes of methamphetamine worth an estimated RM170 million in the Klang Valley. The drugs had reportedly entered through northern Peninsular Malaysia before being stored in rented houses.
In November, police also linked a Hong Kong drug seizure to a syndicate that had used Malaysia as a transit point before the drugs were despatched through KLIA and Penang International Airport.
The challenge is that enforcement cannot be confined to airports. Ports, coastal waters, land crossings, warehouses and logistics facilities all need to be part of a well-coordinated security strategy.
The government's 17-point security improvement and mitigation plan for KLIA and other international entry points is a timely step in the right direction. However, the government will need to ensure that implementation is measurable, adequately funded and continuously evaluated.
We basically need to ensure a fool-proof protective shield covering virtually the entire country, given that an increased security focus on airports will incentivise the drug syndicates to probe for other vulnerable spots along our lengthy coastline as well as land borders.
We simply cannot afford to become a convenient stopover for the international narcotics trade. Our connectivity must be protected at all costs, not exploited. Intelligence gathering and sharing, border screenings and enforcement coordination must all be beefed up without compromising legitimate trade and travel in and out of the country.
There must be no let-up. As the minister rightly said, the police, through the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department, are intensifying efforts against the illicit trade through the entire syndicate network.

Title: Floods forecast in Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin until Wednesday
Article:
KUANTAN: Floods are expected to hit Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin, particularly low-lying areas and flood-prone locations, from today until Wednesday.
The National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre of the Department of Irrigation and Drainage said the forecast followed an alert-level continuous rain warning issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department at 4.30pm today.
In Kuantan, the areas at risk include locations within the Sungai Kuantan Basin, covering Sungai Kuantan, Sungai Lembing, Sungai Kenau, Sungai Beserah, Sungai Belat and Sungai Soi.
Also at risk are areas within the Sungai Cherating Basin (Sungai Cherating), Sungai Pahang Basin (Sungai Lepar) and Sungai Penor Basin (Sungai Penor).
In Pekan, the affected areas are within the Sungai Bebar Basin (Sungai Bebar), Sungai Miang Basin (Sungai Miang), Sungai Pahang Basin (Sungai Pahang, Sungai Pahang Tua and Sungai Mentiga) and Sungai Mercung Basin (Sungai Mercung).
In Rompin, the forecast covers areas within the Sungai Endau Basin (Sungai Endau and Sungai Anak Endau), Sungai Rompin Basin (Sungai Rompin, Sungai Pukin, Sungai Kepasing, Sungai Keratong, Sungai Jeram, Sungai Gayong, Sungai Chanis and Sungai Buan), as well as the Sungai Pontian Pahang Basin (Sungai Pontian Pahang).
"The predicted floods may occur earlier or later than expected.
"This warning is issued to enable all residents, especially those in flood-prone areas, to remain vigilant and comply with instructions from the authorities or flood disaster management agencies," the statement said.

Title: Binance's US$6.3b heist set to trigger tougher insurer scrutiny
Article:
LAST week's US$6.3 billion Binance heist is prompting insurers to scrutinise cryptocurrency companies' security more closely, with underwriters expected to probe if clients are vulnerable to a similar attack when they seek new coverage or renew existing policies, industry insiders and experts said.
Insurers are not expected to broadly retreat from the crypto sector or reduce the availability of coverage.
But the largest crypto theft on record could bring tougher scrutiny of crypto firms' exposure to Binance and any weaknesses identified in the attack, which the Federal Bureau of Investigation has blamed on a North Korea-linked group.
The attack underscores the limits of the insurance coverage available for the fast-growing over US$2.5 trillion industry.
No available crypto insurance could cover a loss of the scale suffered by Binance, experts said, while many policies have exclusions for state-backed cyberattacks.
Grand View Research projects the global crypto insurance market will grow to US$192.7 billion by 2033 from US$13.8 billion this year.
"Insurers will be asking questions specific to Binance. Their first question will be very simple: what is your exposure to them and do you have any money with them?" said David Rogers, managing director of financial institutions at Gallagher.
According to a report that Binance published this week, hackers used a bogus job interview and software hidden in an ​advertisement to compromise the computers of two Binance software engineers before using a third computer to drain US$6.3 billion worth of crypto.
The world's largest crypto exchange detailed a multi-stage hacking endeavour that began in June and set off a series of security breaches culminating in the theft on Thursday.
Following the attack, crypto exchanges quickly moved to bolster their defences and push for greater information-sharing across the industry.
The implications of their insurance will likely become clear at their next renewal, executives said.
Policies typically run for a year, giving underwriters an opportunity to reassess a client's risks, seek updated information and impose new security requirements before agreeing to extend coverage.
Jacqueline Quintal, Marsh's financial institutions and digital asset industry leader, did not anticipate material changes in insurance capacity, pricing or coverage, but for insurers to ask clients more questions, including whether they could be exposed to a similar attack.
She said one would not want to be the person who, a week after this happened, renews or writes a crypto risk and then the same thing happens.
The scrutiny could extend beyond a general assessment of whether cybersecurity controls to specific weaknesses uncovered by the Binance investigation.
Insurers may seek assurances that similar vulnerabilities do not exist elsewhere during renewal.
"If it becomes apparent from the investigation into this hack that there was a very specific weakness or flaw in Binance's security, then other insureds can certainly expect to see a requirement for that weakness or flaw to be resolved," said Peter Hardy, a London-based insurance lawyer at Reed Smith.
The scale of the Binance heist also highlights the limits of the protection available to cryptocurrency businesses.
"A loss of this magnitude prompts underwriters to re-examine their whole crypto book, not just the affected insured, reassessing aggregate exposure, wordings and sub-limits across the portfolio," Alan Lyons, co-chair of the Insurance, Reinsurance & Dispute Resolution Group at Herrick, said.
The predictable response is tighter wordings and clearer exclusions, he said.
North Korea has for years used state-linked cyber units for espionage and financial theft, according to US and South Korean authorities and cybersecurity experts. Pyongyang has denied the allegations.
North Korea's involvement could complicate insurance claims, as cyber policies placed at Lloyd's have generally required exclusions for state-backed attacks since 2023.
The Binance loss also exceeds the capacity of any available policy, he said.
"If an attack is attributed to a state, insurers may dispute or deny claims. The effectiveness of these exclusions in a major, geopolitically driven loss remains untested."
That's a challenge, given the industry is expected to continue expanding with the growth of custody services and wider adoption of cryptocurrencies.
Even multiple policies responding would be insufficient to cover a loss of this scale.
"Potential new entrants to the market may be more cautious but the market will steady itself and in time bounce back," Hardy said.
The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersekutu Bersatu backs proposed appointment of Gerakan member in state assembly
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Terengganu's Bersekutu Bersatu wing has no objection to the state government's proposal to appoint a Gerakan member as an appointed assemblyman.
State Bersekutu Bersatu wing chief Lim Chew Sieng said the proposal to appoint an assemblyman to look after the welfare and interests of non-Muslim communities was raised by the wing two years ago.
He said the state wing welcomed Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar's proposal to appoint a representative from a party within the Perikatan Nasional coalition.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/1573578/terengganu-name-gerakan-member-appointed-assemblyman
He added that such an appointment should have been made in 2025.
"The last time a party representative was appointed as an assemblyman was in 2018, when Zuraida Md Noor, who is now the Ladang assemblyman, was appointed and sworn in for one term that lasted until 2023.
"Although Bersekutu is no longer a member of the PN coalition, we welcome and have no objection to the appointment under Clause 27(2) of the Terengganu State Constitution," he said.
Earlier, Samsuri, who is also PN chairman, announced during a visit to the coalition's operations room in Air Keroh, Melaka, today that a Chinese representative from Gerakan would be appointed as an assemblyman.
Samsuri, who is also Kemaman MP, is expected to propose the appointment at the state executive council meeting next Wednesday.
Lim said appointing a non-Malay representative would give the community a voice in the state assembly.
"Although we are from different parties and Bersekutu is no longer part of the PN coalition, we hope the appointed representative will raise the concerns and interests of non-Muslim communities during state assembly sittings.
"We hope the representative will serve as a bridge to convey the views, needs and interests of these communities to the state government," he said.
Terengganu Gerakan chairman Wong Kim True is understood to be the second appointed assemblyman after Zuraida.

Title: Tensions resurface between Prabowo and predecessor Jokowi
Article:
ACCUSATIONS   of police illegally wiretapping Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and the possible impeachment of his vice-president have exposed fresh tensions in the relationship between Prabowo and his influential predecessor.
Prabowo, a former general with a checkered past, shares a long and complex history with Joko Widodo, the former president better known as Jokowi.
Jokowi defeated Prabowo twice in the 2014 and 2019 presidential elections.
He then appointed Prabowo as defence minister. That helped rebuild Prabowo's reputation after accusations of rights abuses and ended a de facto ban on him travelling to the United States.
Prabowo, who denies any wrongdoing, then won tacit support for his 2024 presidential bid from Jokowi, who was barred by term limits from running again.
Key to that support was his promise to continue Jokowi's legacy projects including building a new capital city, Nusantara.
During that election, Jokowi faced allegations of breaching ethics and meddling ahead of the polls, including in a court's last-minute decision to change election rules, which allowed his son to become Prabowo's running mate.
Jokowi's brother-in-law was head of that court at the time and was reprimanded by an ethics panel for intentionally allowing "intervention from an external party".
Jokowi has rejected those allegations.
In addition to picking Jokowi's son, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, as his running mate, Prabowo installed a number of Jokowi loyalists in his administration in what analysts said was a bid to tap into some of Jokowi's huge support base.
But cracks in their relationship began to appear when he removed or reassigned Jokowi loyalists and technocrats in a series of reshuffles that began in September 2025.
Among those removed was Sri Mulyani Indrawati, who served as Jokowi's finance chief for eight years. More recently, Listyo Sigit Prabowo (no relations to the president), a former police chief who became the president's chief of staff in October, was sacked this week after he was arrested in the wiretapping scandal.
Investigators have not said what they believe is the motive for the wiretapping.
Prabowo has also only approved 48.8 trillion rupiah in funding for the Nusantara project until 2029, about 60 per cent of what Jokowi spent between 2022 and 2024.
In September, a group, including an election monitoring organisation, petitioned the Constitutional Court to review Gibran's eligibility in the 2024 election, arguing that he did not have the appropriate credentials.
There is no apparent connection between the group and Prabowo.
The court last month ruled that Gibran's education diplomas issued overseas did not meet election requirements, but the judges also said he could not be removed from office.
In a separate complaint, the Supreme Court ruled last month that a key education document Gibran used during the election was invalid, according to local media reports. The court has not published its full ruling.
Lawmakers are looking at launching a parliamentary inquiry into the matter, which analysts believe to be the first step towards an impeachment.
According to two people with knowledge of Jokowi's thinking, Jokowi was disappointed that neither Prabowo nor members of his coalition showed any support when questions were raised about Gibran's educational credentials.
Jokowi's assistant did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Gibran also publicly apologised twice that Prabowo's signature free meals for schools programme had resulted in cases of food poisoning — a position that ran counter to the president's, the people said.
The writer is from Reuters

Title: Terengganu to name Gerakan member as appointed assemblyman
Article:
MELAKA: The Terengganu government will appoint a Chinese member of Gerakan as a state assemblyman to represent the community, which currently has no representation in the state assembly.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the proposal had been studied for several months and approved by the Terengganu State Executive Council.
"What I want to say is that we have noted there is no representation from the non-Malay communities in Terengganu.
"I want to announce today that we have agreed to appoint one state assemblyman from the Chinese community because the Terengganu State Constitution has a provision to appoint any race or gender that has no representation," he said.
He made the announcement during a campaign event for the Melaka state election, in a video recorded and posted on Facebook. He was accompanied by Gerakan president Datuk Dr Dominic Lau.
Samsuri said that he had discussed the proposal with Lau several times and gathered the views of other colleagues.
The decision will be finalised at the state assembly sitting on Nov 16 and 17, he said.
"I hope this is good news for everyone, and it is our shared commitment to the Chinese community in Terengganu," Samsuri said.
In a caption accompanying the video, the Terengganu government said the appointment was intended to broaden representation and serve as a bridge between the state government and the state's multiracial communities.
Under Article 27(2) of the Terengganu State Constitution, the state government may appoint up to four assemblymen to represent minority ethnic groups, religions or genders that lack representation among the elected members.

Title: Poland says Austrian woman among killed in Krakow shooting
Article:
KRAKOW: A Polish regional official said on Sunday that an Austrian woman was among the six people killed in a shooting in Krakow after a man opened fire at random in the historic city centre.
"I can confirm that the 51-year-old woman, who is the sixth victim of this attack, is an Austrian national," Malopolska region Governor Krzysztof Kleczar told reporters.
He added that a British citizen whose death in the attack was announced on Saturday was a 32-year-old man. The four others killed were Polish.

Title: Eisenkot given tough task of forming Israeli government to replace Netanyahu
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot was set on Sunday to be given the tough task of forming a government, with weeks to cobble together a coalition to replace Benjamin Netanyahu, the country's longest-serving prime minister.
Eisenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Netanyahu, was due to meet President Isaac Herzog, who will formally give him the mandate to form a government, with an initial deadline of 28 days.
Eisenkot, born to a family of working-class Moroccan immigrants, would be the first Sephardic prime minister — a descendant of Jews from the Middle East or North Africa — in a country long dominated by an Ashkenazi elite with ties to Europe.
Netanyahu, who has been prime minister on and off for nearly two decades and has led wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran since the Oct 7, 2023 attacks, lost support in last month's election, but no side claimed an outright majority.
In consultations with Herzog last week, Eisenkot received recommendations from parties accounting for 67 lawmakers, against 46 for Netanyahu.
But the vote count included Israeli Arabs, whose seat haul surged to a historic high amid anger over Netanyahu's government, which includes far-right firebrands who have openly sought to marginalise the community.
Wooing the ultra-Orthodox
Avigdor Liberman, a former Netanyahu aide turned sharp critic who nonetheless shares his hawkish views, has been adamant against any alliance with Israeli Arabs, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after Israel's creation in 1948.
Taking back one of his signature campaign pledges, Liberman instead voiced openness to an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, whose almost singular priority is ensuring that they remain exempt from military service.
The exemption for the ultra-Orthodox — whose two main parties had been aligned with Netanyahu but could help Eisenkot secure a majority — has been a source of growing resentment among many Israelis as reservists serve multiple tours of duty.
Liberman said on Sunday he still backed conscription for all Israelis but had to make "difficult decisions" in pursuit of the higher priority of ousting Netanyahu, who faces corruption charges that could land him in jail if he loses power.
But he remained adamant that he would never ally with Israeli Arabs.
"I will not lend a hand to the establishment of such a government, which in my view will harm security and bring Netanyahu back to power," Liberman wrote on X.
Liberman, whose party has seven seats and is the smallest within the opposition bloc, denied speculation that he was trying to engineer a deadlock that could result in him becoming prime minister.
Born in Moldova and with a party base originally made up of Russian-speaking immigrants, Liberman said commentators' views on his motives had "sometimes a distinctly racist tone".
Naftali Bennett, the second strongest opposition leader after Liberman, has also been outspoken against the ultra-Orthodox community's military exemption and has remained silent since Liberman's about-face.
'National emergency'
Eisenkot has called for a "national emergency" government that would remove Netanyahu, calling him "a fundamental threat to the very existence of Israeli democracy".
He has ruled out a unity government with Netanyahu, who has repeatedly called for a broad coalition with himself at the helm.
Eisenkot appears to be suggesting that he is willing to start with a minority government — relying on outside votes from Israeli-Arab parties — while continuing to seek a stable government with majority support.
Assaf Shapira, a political expert at the Israel Democracy Institute, said Eisenkot would face an especially fragile government if it had only 48 lawmakers, even if others promised to keep it in power.
"To pass laws, you need strong support from other parties," Shapira said, explaining that an Eisenkot minority government would be forced into extensive negotiations on every piece of legislation.
Eisenkot has vowed to repair Israel's international reputation and put an end to rampant violence against Palestinians by extremist West Bank settlers supported by Netanyahu's government.
He has warned Netanyahu that he does not have the mandate for another attack on Iran but has also largely backed his war decisions.
Having commanded the military during the 2006 war with Hizbollah, Eisenkot devised the so-called "Dahiya doctrine", which calls for massive force against civilian infrastructure where enemies operate — a policy critics say amounts to a war crime.
In Tel Aviv, Neri Bar-On, who works in educational technology, said he expected Eisenkot to succeed in forming a government.
"But the problems run deeper," he said.
"The country is facing a massive internal conflict; even if he manages to form a government, it won't solve the underlying issues."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four firearms seized at Krakow shooting scene, seven at gunman's home
Article:
MOSCOW: Four firearms were seized at the scene of a shooting in the Polish city of Krakow, while another seven were found at the gunman's home, Kielce District Prosecutor Daniel Prokopowicz said on Sunday, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
"Seven firearms and a large quantity of ammunition were seized at the shooter's residence. Four weapons were recovered at the crime scene in Krakow," Prokopowicz told reporters.
The seizures were consistent with information from law enforcement agencies that the shooter and his father held permits for a total of 11 firearms, the prosecutor said.
The shooter himself had a permit for two firearms, he added.
On Saturday evening, Polish police said an unidentified individual had opened fire from a moving car in central Krakow.
Police later reported that six people had been killed and 16 others injured, including police officers.
The wounded assailant was detained and remains in hospital.
The bodies of the shooter's sister and parents were subsequently discovered during a search of his home.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Deepavali cheer across borders
Article:
LETTER:
This is my third year not being able to celebrate Deepavali at home, in a part of the United Kingdom where the festival is not even routinely known or recognised.
I found myself on the couch at half past 10 in the evening, Greenwich Mean Time, tucked under a blanket because it is miserably cold, scrolling through YouTube.
And what do i find but a repost by Petronas. Their Deepavali advertisement from 2003.
It was quite a sensation back then, and remains one of their most memorable.
The one where Patti innocently asks Sam, in Tamil, what sort of a name Sam is, only for him to reveal that his actual name is Muthusamy Karrupiah.
I was eleven back then. A primary school pupil. My father was still alive and well. I had no ambitions, no financial obligations or worries. I was simply a child.
Now, over two decades later, I am a grown adult, navigating the uncertainties of life as an international medical graduate trying to build a life in the UK.
Rewatching it brought back memories of a better time.
Of those halcyon days, as one would say, when life seemed so much simpler and the people i loved were still around.
And the message at the end? "The world is changing, but we will always be proud of who we are."
As an 11-year-old, i probably never gave those words a second thought. As an adult, I finally understand what they mean.
I am proud to call myself a Malaysian Tamil, and that will remain my identity no matter where life takes me. Living abroad also made me realise how much of myself remains rooted in the country i call home.
Perhaps that is the strange thing about growing older. Things that once seemed insignificant acquire an entirely different meaning when revisited through the eyes of an adult.
An advertisement that once interrupted my grandmother's favourite Tamil serial has, 23 years later, become something that reminds me of home, my father, my childhood and the Malaysia I left behind.
I may be far from home, but my heart is there tonight. And I thank Petronas, one of our national prides, for sharing it again.
It brought a little Deepavali cheer to a Malaysian spending yet another festive season away from home.
'Selamat Hari Deepavali' to everyone celebrating, including Malaysians who, like me, are spending the festival far away from home.
LOSHI RAJEN
Merseyside, England
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Couple posing as police personnel caught by villagers in Dungun
Article:
DUNGUN: A husband and wife who posed as police personnel to extort an elderly woman were cornered and caught by villagers at Felda Rasau Kerteh 3 around 4pm today.
The incident began when the victim, Mariani Ismail, 64, received a video call from one of the suspects, who was dressed in a police uniform against a background resembling the Kuantan district police headquarters.
Frightened after being threatened and falsely accused of wrongdoing, Mariani handed over three pieces of jewellery worth thousands of ringgit on Nov 6.
After realising she had been duped in the first incident, Mariani lodged a police report, allowing her family and villagers to stay alert and monitor the suspects' movements.
The suspects returned to her house today to demand an additional RM50,000 in cash.
Mariani's husband, Zakaria Ibrahim, said the suspects initially acted cautiously and refused to enter the house.
"Instead, they instructed us to place the RM50,000 in the mailbox in front of our house.
"However, I lured them by asking them to collect the money themselves from the car," he said.
The plan worked, with villagers who had been waiting around the house quickly surrounding the two suspects.
"The two foreign suspects are believed to have pawned my wife's jewellery at a gold shop in Kuala Lumpur for nearly RM13,000.
"They were then taken to the Dungun district police headquarters to assist in investigations. I understand they will be remanded at the Dungun magistrate's court tomorrow," he said.

Title: Malaysian suspect arrested with 102kg syabu in Brunei was en route to Sabah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The man arrested with more than 100kg of syabu at the Brunei-Miri border in Sarawak on Oct 31 was a Malaysian believed to be travelling to Sabah.
Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the 46-year-old suspect was from Miri, Sarawak, and had two previous criminal records.
"Police received information from Brunei's Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) regarding the arrest of a Malaysian man by Brunei Customs at the Sungai Tujoh Control Post.
"Preliminary investigations based on information from the NCB found that the suspect was arrested while entering Brunei from Miri, Sarawak," he said when contacted.
Hussein said information from the Brunei authorities indicated that the suspect was believed to have used the country as a transit route before re-entering Malaysia.
"The suspect was expected to travel through Kuala Belait, Seria, Tutong and Bandar Seri Begawan before heading to Temburong via the Sultan Haji Omar 'Ali Saifuddien Bridge.
"He was then expected to re-enter Sarawak through Labu-Mengkalap before heading to Sabah via the Merapok-Sindumin route," he said.
He said the seized drugs, believed to be syabu, weighed an estimated 100kg and were worth about RM5 million.
Hussein said the department would continue intelligence cooperation with the NCB to identify the source of the drugs and possible links to syndicate networks in Malaysia.
"The department will continue intelligence coordination and cooperation with the NCB to obtain information on the source of the drugs.
"This cooperation is also aimed at identifying the possible involvement of individuals or drug trafficking syndicate networks linked to Malaysia," he said.
Earlier, Brunei authorities reported
the seizure of 102.19kg of syabu
concealed in 100 tea packets at the Sungai Tujoh Control Post along the Brunei-Miri border.
The drugs were estimated to be worth at least BND2.8 million, making it the largest drug seizure recorded at the control post.
Besides syabu, Brunei authorities also seized four Erimin 5 pills, RM1,180, S$10, BND10 and 500 baht in cash, two mobile phones and a vehicle believed to have been used in the operation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Train collision in Egypt's Giza injures 120
Article:
CAIRO: Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages and injuring at least 120 people, state newspaper Al-Akhbar Al-Youm reported.
Egypt's railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.
Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said.
Egypt's Health Ministry said 52 ambulances were dispatched to the scene and the injured were taken to two nearby hospitals.
Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza's Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt's worst-ever rail disaster.
In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holidaymakers south of Cairo.
In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.
Egypt's 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents.
Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

Title: Melaka Chetti community keeps Deepavali traditions alive
Article:
MELAKA: Deepavali celebrations by the Melaka Chetti community at Kampung Chetti had a distinctively festive atmosphere, with the Festival of Lights marked by a spirit of goodwill, harmony and family togetherness.
Although only about 30 families are believed to remain in the heritage village, the lively celebrations, marked by unique traditions, demonstarted the minority community's efforts to safeguard its identity, which dates back to the era of the Melaka Sultanate.
One tradition that sets the community apart from other Hindu communities is the practice of temple priests delivering prasadam and visiting homes to bless families.
However, public understanding and knowledge of the unique culture and history of the Melaka Chetti community remain limited, particularly among those outside the community, leading to misconceptions about its true identity.
Among those working to preserve its heritage is Wenila Nadarajan, 46, who is determined to ensure the community's continued presence in Malaysia, particularly in Melaka.
Wenila, who runs a Chetti food business in Jalan Tengkera, described herself as often playing the role of a storyteller to answer questions from the public about the origins of the Indian Peranakan community, which practises Hinduism but speaks a form of Malay creole.
"At my shop, I am like a storyteller. Whenever people come, I have to explain who the Chetti people are because they do not know. Many people, especially those from outside Melaka, are unfamiliar with the community.
"Many assume that the Chetti community is Muslim because they speak Malay, or because they do not know how to speak Tamil, although that is not the case for everyone.
"In the past, the Chetti community spoke Baba Malay, but nowadays many also marry Indians and Chinese, so the language has become a mixture," she told Bernama at her home here.
Wenila also hopes that efforts to promote and raise awareness of the Chetti Melaka community, including through school history textbooks, can be expanded so that younger generations become more familiar with its existence.
However, beneath the pride in the community's distinctive identity and traditions lies deep concern over the future of the heritage village, which is increasingly threatened by rapid development.
A native of the village, Shanmugam Raja, 57, said the historic settlement must be protected from physical development that could wipe out the community's culture.
"This place should be preserved. If the village is not gazetted and uncontrolled development is allowed, it will affect the settlement. If the village disappears, the Chetti community, along with our culture and heritage, will quickly become extinct and be lost.
"One thing I have observed is that when members of a community do not live together in one area, practising their culture and traditions is not difficult, but there is a lack of encouragement.
"Here, all the neighbours practise them together, making it easier and more enjoyable," he said.
The information technology professional also expressed concern about younger generations who move away and later return to the village with the mindset of being 'guests' rather than 'hosts', consequently reducing their sense of responsibility towards carrying on their customs and traditions.
"I have noticed that many among the younger generation, when they return, do not see themselves as hosts but as guests. When this happens, they do not take part in the activities here.
"That is the problem, and over time, these cultural practices will disappear," he said.

Title: Man held over alleged rape of 14-year-old niece in Besut
Article:
BESUT: Police have arrested a 40-year-old man to assist in investigations into the alleged rape of his 14-year-old niece.
Besut police chief Superintendent Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said police received a report on the case today before arresting the local man at his home in Kampung Raja at 2.45pm.
He said a urine screening test found that the suspect tested positive for methamphetamine.
"The suspect also has 11 previous records involving drug-related and other criminal offences," he said in a statement.
The victim told a family member about the incident before a police report was lodged.
The case is being investigated under Section 376 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of up to 30 years and whipping upon conviction.
Rozaime said police viewed all forms of sexual crime involving children seriously.
"Parents and guardians are advised to remain vigilant about their children's safety and immediately report any form of abuse or sexual harassment to the police," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia calls for stronger cybersecurity, child online safety
Article:
DOHA: Malaysia has emphasised the need to strengthen cybersecurity and protect children online while ensuring the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said trust and safety were essential to enabling people to participate confidently in the digital economy, as technological advancements continued to reshape the way people lived and worked.
He said Malaysia welcomed the draft Doha Ministerial Declaration, which outlined a comprehensive approach to addressing the opportunities and challenges of digital transformation.
"The Declaration rightly puts a strong focus on cybersecurity, protecting children online, and ensuring that emerging technologies are developed and used responsibly.
"For Malaysia, innovation must go hand in hand with the right safeguards. This will give people the confidence to make full use of the opportunities that digital technologies offer," he said at the Ministerial Roundtable held in conjunction with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26).
He said the declaration reflected three priorities central to Malaysia's national digital agenda, which were ensuring meaningful connectivity, promoting digital inclusion and fostering a safe and trusted digital environment.
He said meaningful connectivity must go beyond network coverage to ensure that telecommunications services remain affordable, reliable and resilient in supporting communities and economic activities.
Malaysia also welcomed the declaration's emphasis on developing resilient and sustainable digital infrastructure to ensure the continuity of essential communications during emergencies and disruptions.
Fahmi said digital transformation must create opportunities for everyone regardless of geographical location or level of digital readiness.
He added that the Malaysian government remained focused on investing in digital skills and capacity building while supporting innovation to enable more people to benefit from the digital economy.
"As AI and other emerging technologies continue to develop, we must make sure that developing countries and underserved communities are not left behind.
"They should have the opportunity not only to use these technologies, but also to help shape them and benefit from the opportunities they create," he said.
Fahmi also welcomed the declaration's emphasis on international cooperation and acknowledged the ITU's important role in expanding connectivity, developing technical standards and strengthening digital capacity.
He said Malaysia looked forward to working closely with the ITU and other member states to build a more connected and inclusive digital future while ensuring greater safety and equitable opportunities for all.

Title: Nine remanded over fatal brawl that killed teenager in Sibu
Article:
SIBU: Nine suspects have been remanded for seven days until Nov 15 to assist in investigations into the stabbing of a 19-year-old man during a brawl yesterday.
Sibu police chief assistant commissioner Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the suspects, aged between 16 and 42, were brought to court at 7.15am today for the remand application.
He said a post-mortem examination completed today found that the victim died from chest injuries.
"The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code," he said.
The Sibu district police headquarters Criminal Investigation Department launched an operation to track down those believed to be involved after receiving a report about 2am yesterday.
All nine suspects were arrested at several locations around Sibu between 10am and 4pm yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 20-year-old man drowns while swimming at Taiping waterfall
Article:
IPOH: A 20-year-old man drowned while swimming with four friends at Taman Suria Waterfall near Taiping this afternoon.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said teams from the Taiping and Kamunting fire and rescue stations were dispatched to the scene after receiving a distress call at 2.10pm.
"Upon the arrival at the scene, it was found that the victim had been taken out of the water by his friends," he said in a statement.
Sabarodzi said firefighters performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on the victim, but he was pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry personnel.
"The victim's body was handed over to the police for further action, and the operation ended at 4.20pm," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two policemen hurt after patrol car overturns avoiding monkeys
Article:
KUALA BERANG: Two policemen were injured when their patrol car skidded and overturned several times while trying to avoid a group of monkeys in the middle of the road at Kilometer 4 of Jalan Simpang Bukit Kepah–Tapah, Kampung Kepah, this evening.
Hulu Terengganu police chief Superintendent Sharudin Abdul Wahab said police received information about the accident about 4.30pm.
The driver, Muhammad Amirul Hafiz Ahmad, 26, suffered a fracture to his left arm, while his colleague, Khairil Azlan Abdul Latif, 44, sustained jaw pain.
He said both officers from the Hulu Terengganu district police headquarters' Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Division were on patrol duty when the incident occurred.
"Their Honda City patrol car was travelling from Simpang Kepah towards Kuala Berang when they encountered a group of monkeys in the middle of the road.
"Initial investigations found that the driver tried to avoid the animals by steering to the right, but lost control of the vehicle, causing it to skid and overturn several times," he said.
The officers were taken to Hulu Terengganu Hospital by an ambulance from the Civil Defence Force for further treatment.
Sharudin said investigations found that the accident occurred along a bend, where the road surface was wet from rain.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Plane hits pickup truck during emergency landing in Florida
Article:
MOSCOW: A small Cessna 172D Skyhawk aircraft crashed into a moving pickup truck while attempting an emergency landing in Florida, US, Lee County Sheriff Carmine Marceno said, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
"The pilots attempted an emergency landing. During the landing, the aircraft crashed into the rear of a pickup truck," Marceno wrote on the social media platform X on Saturday.
The aircraft had developed a mechanical malfunction, the sheriff said. Two pilots were on board.
An investigation led by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is under way, he added.
The incident occurred around midday local time on Saturday in North Fort Myers, near Interstate 75, Fox News reported.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man dies after falling from 23rd floor of Bayan Lepas hotel
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 25-year-old man died after falling from the 23rd floor of a hotel in Bayan Lepas.
Northeast acting police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police were alerted to the incident at 7.13am following a report from the public.
"A hotel employee discovered the victim lying face down and covered in blood on the ground floor about 6.40am.
"Initial investigations indicate that the victim, who was from Bayan Lepas, is suspected to have fallen from a balcony on the 23rd floor of the building," he said in a statement.
Abdul Rozak said crime scene and forensic examinations found no signs of foul play.
"A post-mortem examination conducted by a forensic specialist at Penang Hospital confirmed that the deceased suffered severe injuries to his legs, body and head consistent with a fall from height, with no indications of criminal elements," he added.
The case has been classified as sudden death, and a sudden death report has been opened for further investigation.

Title: Isa Isarb: 'We were detained over spy suspicions during Indonesia haze shoot'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Social media influencer Isa Isarb and his team were detained by Indonesian authorities while filming a haze documentary in the country recently, after they were suspected of being spies from Malaysia.
In a statement posted on social media, Isa Isarb, whose real name is Isa Batharul Zaman, 28, said authorities also suspected them of receiving funds from certain parties to topple a government.
He said their actual purpose in visiting Indonesia was to film a documentary on the haze.
"On the day of the incident, we were on our way to an area where a forest fire had occurred when we saw a crowd gathering at a student demonstration.
"We stopped to interview some of them. Not long after, 10 to 15 Indonesian authorities approached us. One of them asked whether I was Isa Batharul, although I am better known as Isa Isarb," he said.
He said they sensed something was amiss before being detained for allegedly misusing their tourist visas.
"Based on the explanation given, the visa did not allow us to film or be at a demonstration site.
"At the police station, I was asked to unlock my phone and explain the purpose of our visit to Indonesia. I fully cooperated throughout the questioning before we spent the night in a lock-up," he said.
He said he became anxious the following day when about 40 more personnel, including members of the cyber security team equipped with advanced technology and senior officers whose identities were unclear, arrived at the initially quiet police station.
He feared they could become victims of circumstances or be made scapegoats for certain parties.
"The next morning, I was told we were suspected of being spies from Malaysia because there was evidence of conversations with several Malaysian politicians.
"The conversations referred to were between me and the teams of the deputy prime minister, Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. They were simply arrangements to invite them for interviews for the haze documentary we were filming," he said.
He said an invitation to parliament during the same week had further complicated matters during questioning, although the purpose was to interview the MP.
"The location was chosen to accommodate his busy schedule, especially as he had just got married.
"We were terrified at the thought of facing 20 years in prison or death by firing squad if convicted of espionage," he said.
He said they spent the next six days in fear and were questioned daily, to the point where they felt they had run out of hope.
He also described missing his wife and child while worrying about their future if he were sentenced in Indonesia.
"I tried to calm myself by drawing their faces on the lock-up wall using a metal pin from the detention notice given to me.
"On some nights, I suffered panic attacks because I felt trapped within four walls, not knowing what awaited me the next day," he said.
He said they were eventually able to return home, thanks to the good relations between the Indonesian and Malaysian governments.
He thanked the Indonesian government for treating them fairly throughout the investigation and the Malaysian government for assisting them when needed.
He hoped to share more details of the experience as a lesson to others, but did not want the incident to be used as campaign material or for anyone's political interests.

Title: Krakow gunman's parents and sister found dead at family home
Article:
WARSAW: The three people found dead at the home of the gunman who opened fire in Krakow's main square on Saturday were his parents and sister, Polish radio station RMF FM reported on Sunday, citing police.
The station quoted police spokesman Andrzej Fijolek, according to German Press Agency (dpa).
The bodies were discovered during a police operation at the 24-year-old gunman's home in the town of Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, about a two-hour drive north-east of Krakow.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk had earlier said they were believed to be members of the gunman's immediate family.
The man drove his car into Krakow's busy market square on Saturday and opened fire indiscriminately at passers-by.
According to official figures, six people were killed and 16 injured, several of them seriously or critically.
His motive remained unclear, but Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said on Saturday that initial findings suggested the suspect held "very radical views."
President Karol Nawrocki declared two days of national mourning on Sunday and Monday.
One of the fatalities was a British citizen, the PAP news agency reported, citing a police spokesman.
It added that five of the injured were nationals of Germany, Britain, Portugal, Russia and Austria.
Two police officers and the perpetrator were also among those injured.
Krakow is a popular tourist destination, with its market square and Renaissance buildings among the city's main attractions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang police address claims girl was returned to alleged abuser's home
Article:
BALIK PULAU: Penang police have clarified details of a child sexual assault case involving an 11-year-old girl after an assemblyman raised concerns over her welfare and protection.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said the Southwest district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Division received a report from a school principal at 11.15am on Oct 16, 2025.
The report concerned allegations that the girl had been sexually assaulted by her biological father.
Acting on the report, police arrested the girl's father about 5.30pm the same day. He was remanded until Oct 24, 2025.
The suspect was charged at the Balik Pulau court on Oct 24, 2025, under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, read together with Section 16 of the same Act.
The case is currently on trial, with the next court date scheduled for Nov 11, 2026.
On the girl's welfare, Lim said she was initially placed under her grandmother's temporary care on Oct 16, 2025, as her biological mother was in Singapore at the time.
"On Oct 17, 2025, the victim was referred to the One Stop Crisis Centre (OSCC) at Penang Hospital and warded in the paediatric ward until Oct 21, 2025.
"The Southwest district Welfare Department then handed the victim over to her biological mother on Oct 21, 2025," he said.
Lim advised the public not to speculate or spread unverified information that could lead to misunderstandings concerning the case.
His statement followed Berapit assemblyman Heng Lee Lee's recent questioning of why the girl, who was allegedly sexually abused by her biological father, was allowed to return to an environment where the alleged perpetrator resided instead of being placed under immediate state protection.
Heng described the incident as a breakdown in systemic safeguards, citing what she said were significant coordination failures among the police, hospitals and the Welfare Department.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Philippines rebukes officials over public comments about China
Article:
MANILA: The Philippines' Foreign Ministry issued a rare rebuke to government officials and agencies on Sunday over public comments about China, stressing the need for a unified voice as the country prepares to host a key regional summit.
The Philippines' uniformed services have been engaged in a long-running war of words with the Chinese government over the South China Sea, a busy waterway that Beijing claims almost entirely despite an international ruling that its position has no legal basis.
Multiple senators also called last month for Beijing's ambassador to be declared persona non grata after he suggested China could "easily win" any confrontation with the Philippines.
Beijing subsequently accused Manila of "erecting multiple obstacles" to its attendance at an Asean defence ministers' meeting, pointedly sending only an embassy defence attaché.
"Public statements that undermine the government's diplomatic approach do more than complicate the work of our diplomats," the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said, without specifying particular incidents.
"They risk eroding the country's credibility in international affairs and project an image of internal division that external parties can exploit. Such actions can ultimately weaken the Philippines' negotiating position."
The statement specifically addressed the country's national security establishment and uniformed services, which have engaged in months of heated exchanges with the Chinese Embassy on social media.
US ally the Philippines has been engaged in years of confrontations with China at sea over disputed areas of the strategic waterway, with repeated incidents occurring in recent months.
Sunday's statement said that while the armed services were indispensable in documenting incidents, "civilian authority directs the country's international relations".
It noted that the 2016 international court verdict that broadly dismissed China's claims to the South China Sea came through "rigorous legal proceedings under international law, not through public messaging or social media".
Defence Minister Gilberto Teodoro was banned from visiting China this year, with Beijing citing "irresponsible remarks".
Chester Cabalza, a Manila-based security analyst, said the Foreign Ministry had gone public with its message to "assure its counterparts, particularly China, that they are in control of the Philippines' foreign policy".
"(The defence department and coast guard) are obliged to carve out the security policy of the country but not its foreign policy. DFA's statement is an assertion of their role in the bureaucracy."
China's top diplomat, Wang Yi, urged the Philippines in a phone call with his counterpart Theresa Lazaro last week to rein in politicians who had "smeared" Beijing and crossed its "red lines".
Lazaro called the conversation "frank and constructive", adding that "both sides emphasised the need for continued diplomatic dialogue and the proper management of differences anchored on mutual respect".
Manila is set to host a major Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit next week, with attendees to include US President Donald Trump and recently re-elected Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
Beijing has yet to announce publicly whom it will send.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man arrested 12 hours after stealing RM500 from Rembau mosque
Article:
REMBAU: A man was arrested about 12 hours after stealing RM500 from a mosque donation box in Kampung Seberang Batu Hampar, early today.
Rembau police chief Superintendent Ngiam Ooi Ming said police received a report on the break-in at 9.03am.
"The incident is believed to have occurred between 2am and 4.30am.
"The suspect forced open the mosque's rear sliding door before prying open and cutting the padlocks on three donation boxes," she said in a statement.
She said the loss was estimated around RM500.
Acting on information, a team from the Rembau district police headquarters arrested a man around 2.20pm.
"The case is being investigated under Section 457 of the Penal Code.
"The suspect, who is in his 20s, will be brought to the Seremban magistrate's court tomorrow morning for a remand application to facilitate investigations," she said.

Title: Drain overflow causes flash floods in Taman Sri Muda — Fire and Rescue Dept
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Overflowing drains caused flash floods in several areas around Section 25, Taman Sri Muda, Jalan Kebun, Kampung Baru Hicom in Section 26 and Section 13 here today.
Heavy rain from 3.15pm caused water to accumulate in several flood-prone areas.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the Shah Alam Fire and Rescue Station reported that water levels were beginning to recede after the rain stopped.
"Selangor Fire and Rescue Department personnel are continuing to monitor flood-prone locations, and no evacuations have been carried out in the affected areas," he told the media.
He advised residents to remain cautious amid unpredictable weather conditions.
Photographs shared by the department showed floodwaters reaching about halfway up the tyres of cars in Taman Sri Muda and Kampung Baru Hicom between 3.48pm and 3.57pm, before beginning to recede shortly afterwards.

Title: 'Trump has cost us': After midterm losses, MAGA asks if it's over
Article:
DALLAS: As Republicans faced a nationwide drubbing in Tuesday's midterm elections, supporters streamed out of a Dallas ballroom where they had hoped to toast a win for US Senate candidate Ken Paxton, a favourite of President Donald Trump.
In the hotel bar, Michael Little, a 59-year-old businessman and three-time Trump voter, stared at the president's image on a television screen.
"People are pissed off at Trump. Trump has cost us," he said, capturing a sentiment rippling through the president's Make America Great Again movement after the Republican Party's worst electoral defeat in decades.
Across the coalition, some supporters who once viewed Trump as MAGA's greatest asset are beginning to question whether he has become its biggest liability.
Still, the midterm losses amounted to more than a repudiation of Trump. They were a referendum on the political and cultural movement he built.
A defining force in American politics that began as a campaign slogan during Trump's 2016 presidential run now faces a potentially existential reckoning after voters disillusioned with soaring fuel prices, the Iran war and corruption in Washington delivered Democrats decisive congressional majorities.
Trump's first major response to the midterms came on Friday. Instead of changing course, he doubled down on the movement's core. He promoted Stephen Miller, the main architect of the administration's hardline immigration crackdown, to chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Wiles was seen as a stabilising force inside an often chaotic White House.
The move was celebrated by some of MAGA's most ardent influencers, who saw it as a return to the anti-immigration agenda at the movement's roots. "Exactly the energy we need," right-wing influencer Benny Johnson posted on X to his 4.1 million followers. "Solid move. It's Miller Time."
The White House did not directly answer Reuters' questions about why Republicans lost, the defeat of candidates who embraced Trump's false 2020 election claims, or where MAGA goes from here. Instead, it pointed to Trump's remarks on Wednesday, when he said, "If I were on the ballot, we would have won." He also said it was "largely true" that the Iran war had cost Republicans because "it drove the gasoline up", but that he would do it again.
For nearly a decade, MAGA has reshaped the Republican Party and transformed national debates on issues such as trade, immigration, race and gender.
The movement installed loyalists throughout federal agencies, cracked down on immigration and pressured corporations and public institutions to retreat from diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives.
MAGA survived the fallout from the Jan 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol and propelled Trump back to the White House. Now, the Democrats' sweeping victory has forced the movement to grapple with an unexpected question: Is MAGA over?
Reuters interviews with more than a dozen MAGA activists, influencers, party strategists, Christian nationalist leaders and researchers who track right-wing politics, along with a review of MAGA supporters' posts and podcasts since Tuesday, show a movement turning its anger on itself.
The stolen-election claims that have driven MAGA since Democrat Joe Biden beat Trump in the 2020 presidential election have mostly gone quiet.
Instead, supporters are blaming Republican leaders and Trump's advisers, and in some cases the president himself, for broken promises on living costs, the Iran war and the government's decision to redact or withhold major portions of its investigative files on late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
MAGA's factions also disagree about what comes next. Some want a return to populist and nationalist basics. Some want a movement less tied to one man. And a vocal minority say MAGA is already dead.
"We have to rebuild," Steve Bannon, a prominent MAGA proponent, podcaster and former Trump White House adviser, told Reuters. He urged the party to double down on an aggressive populist and nationalist agenda and praised Trump for elevating Miller.
"Miller's appointment as chief of staff underpins my point," he said. "There is no more hardcore MAGA proponent than Stephen."
As pro-Trump internet forums digested the election results, a notable slice of self-described MAGA loyalists — more than 20 per cent — raised doubts about the movement's leadership and direction, according to an analysis of social media traffic done for Reuters by PeakMetrics, a data intelligence firm.
About half of that cohort remained supportive of the MAGA movement but no longer backed Trump as its leader. The other half remained loyal to, though critical of, the president himself.
The analysis was based on 12,850 posts sampled from a universe of 4.6 million Trump-related comments on X and Reddit from 9pm on Election Day to 8pm the next evening. It found broad concern among MAGA supporters as the results became clear.
Of the posts that assigned blame for the rout, nearly a third said concerns about the Iran war and Israel's influence over US policy had overshadowed Trump's message. A quarter said Republicans not fully committed to the MAGA agenda had undermined the movement.
The results left Trump facing large Democratic majorities in both chambers of Congress. In the Senate, Democrats could control as many as 56 of the chamber's 100 seats, more than enough to block Trump's future judicial picks.
Republicans might not be able to recapture the Senate until 2032, Republican Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said the morning after the election.
"It's the political equivalent of a meteor strike that went all around the United States," DeSantis said at a post-election briefing.
Democrats will now control governorships in seven battleground states Trump won in 2024 and, strikingly, they won every statewide race in Texas, which has not backed a Democratic presidential candidate since 1976.
[[nid:1573549]]
MAGA is stale
Since Tuesday, talk of election fraud has virtually vanished among right-wing influencers.
"I have been banging the drum of rigged and stolen elections since 2020, but that is not why we lost the midterms," Rogan O'Handley, a MAGA influencer who posts under the name DC_Draino, wrote on X to his 2.3 million followers.
"We lost because we failed to fix the things voters sent us to do." He did not respond to a request for comment.
After the 2020 election, Trump supporter Isabella DeLuca was among thousands who stormed the US Capitol on Jan 6, 2021. She was charged with five crimes, including theft of a table from inside the Capitol, and pleaded not guilty. Her case was dismissed after Trump returned to office and pardoned her.
This time, the 26-year-old conservative influencer directed her anger towards what she described as out-of-touch Republican leaders who failed to appeal to Gen Z voters on affordability, avoiding foreign wars and other key issues.
"Republicans were just lazy. They felt like that they were entitled to people's votes and that people would vote for them no matter what," DeLuca told Reuters. "It goes to show you that you do have to earn people's votes, and that even in a super red state like Texas, you're not untouchable."
The MAGA movement this year appeared "tired", she said.
That sentiment was echoed in online right-wing forums, said Jennifer Golbeck, a University of Maryland professor who has analysed MAGA-related posts since 2016. She said engagement by Trump's most loyal backers has steadily declined since January, including a 27 per cent drop in posts and comments on Patriots.Win, a popular MAGA forum.
"The enthusiasm and the passion even among this hardest core group of supporters hasn't really been there," Golbeck said. "They are saying that 'MAGA is stale.' It's not new and exciting like it once was."
Fox News, a cable network that has long been a key platform for MAGA voices, saw a sharp decline in viewership ahead of the midterms, with its total daytime audience down 27 per cent in October from a year earlier, according to Nielsen, the audience measurement firm.
In a statement to Reuters, Fox said it drew more viewers than its cable-news rivals on election night. "FOX News has been the number one network in cable news for a quarter century," spokesperson Caley Cronin said.
Some prominent right-wing influencers blamed the president's advisers or Republican lawmakers — but rarely Trump himself — for ignoring key voter concerns. In posts, online broadcasts and interviews with Reuters, many blamed dissatisfaction with the economy, though they differed on other reasons for Tuesday's results.
It wasn't just failure to address affordability that "crushed" Republicans, said Ben Shapiro, co-founder of the conservative site Daily Wire, on his online show on Wednesday. "If you're talking about an electoral catastrophe — a wipeout like we saw last night — you need more ingredients. Here are the other ingredients: chaos and corruption."
Laura Loomer, an influencer close to Trump, wrote on X: "America is over and the American Dream is dead." Yet she told Reuters the losses did not signal the end of MAGA, arguing that anyone seeking the 2028 Republican presidential nomination would need Trump's base.
"The Republican Party belongs to President Trump," Loomer said. "The MAGA movement is still the majority of the GOP base, and whoever wants to run for president in 2028 on the GOP ticket, they would be unwise to be dismissive of President Trump."
On Thursday, Loomer put her podcast on hiatus, saying she had been "running on empty for too long" and needed to focus on her personal life and upcoming wedding. She would return in January, she added.
[[nid:1573548]]
Broken promises
The midterms also tested the beliefs that have held MAGA together, and some of them are giving way.
The Democratic sweep dealt a significant setback to the election denial movement, a central pillar of MAGA politics since Trump's 2020 defeat. Candidates who embraced his false claims of widespread voter fraud lost heavily, including several who had worked to overturn the 2020 result.
Election deniers will hold at least 41 fewer congressional and statewide offices next year, and they have lost 70 per cent of the called races for statewide posts that oversee elections, according to States United Action, a non-profit that tracks such candidates.
Trump made no effort to contest the results and instead blamed Republicans for the defeat.
With few close races and no credible basis for a challenge, many prominent pro-Trump election sceptics dropped fraud allegations and urged supporters to keep organising. A handful of allies still alleged, without evidence, that the vote was rigged.
Mike Lindell, the MyPillow founder and promoter of false claims that machines flipped votes in 2020, said he was not concerned by Trump's pledge to accept the results. "That's his opinion. I've got a different opinion," Lindell told Reuters. "I think it's all been stolen."
But such claims stayed largely on the fringe, even among Republicans. Without contested races, the MAGA election denial movement risks losing the money, attention and momentum that sustained it. "Nobody's going to be putting money behind it," said Wendy Via, co-founder of the Global Project Against Hate and Extremism, a non-profit that tracks hate speech and extremism.
Retired Lieutenant General Mike Flynn, who falsely claimed the 2020 election was stolen and is a popular figure in the Christian nationalist wing of the MAGA movement, accepted the defeat. He called the results "a massacre" and criticised Trump and his administration for failing to deliver on pledges ranging from lowering costs to releasing the government's investigative files on Epstein.
Responding to Vice President JD Vance's assessment on X that the Iran war was "the reason we lost", Flynn wrote: "the sheer number of broken promises is why the blue tsunami happened."
Flynn also criticised Christian voters for failing to show up. "As a Catholic and a Christian, I'm sorely embarrassed and disappointed," he wrote.
Other prominent Christian nationalists were divided over whether MAGA can outlast Trump.
Douglas Wilson, a Christian nationalist pastor who was invited by US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to deliver a sermon at the Pentagon in February, told Reuters that MAGA "is not going anywhere" but must become less personality-driven and more focused on border control, tax cuts and avoiding foreign wars.
Joel Webbon, a far-right Christian nationalist pastor from Texas, was far less sanguine. "Trump lost this all by himself," he said in a video on X, arguing that the president abandoned his base by embracing Israel, launching the war in Iran and failing to follow through on releasing the Epstein files and mass deportations.
"MAGA is dead," Webbon wrote in an accompanying post. "Forever."
