Title: BN-Perikatan cooperation may not translate into full voter support, says Melaka Pakatan chairman
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — Cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the 16th Melaka state election does not guarantee a full transfer of votes between their supporters, despite the apparent advantage of such an arrangement on paper.
State Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari said supporters of the two coalitions might not necessarily embrace the cooperation, while new voters could also influence the election outcome.
He said some voters had chosen PN in previous elections because they did not want to support BN, and the cooperation could therefore affect their existing support base.
“The same applies to BN. For example, based on the Negeri Sembilan state election results, the highest vote transfer rate recorded was 70 per cent.
“This means that the remaining 30 per cent of BN votes might not go to PN. In Melaka, however, the rate could be 60 or even 50 per cent, depending on how supporters of both coalitions respond to the cooperation,” he said after attending a Ziarah Kasih programme at Rumah Awam Bukit Beruang here today.
Adly was responding to a question about his confidence in retaining the Bukit Katil seat in the state election.
Elaborating further, the former Melaka chief minister said the nearly 4,000 new voters in Bukit Katil could also influence voting patterns, as most had no strong allegiance to any political party.
He said Bukit Katil was a mixed constituency, with Malays accounting for about 65 per cent of voters, followed by Chinese (29 per cent) and Indians (five per cent).
He added that playing on racial and religious sentiments to win votes did not guarantee support from voters whose loyalties were divided among several political parties.
“In the previous state election, Malay support for PH exceeded 27 per cent, and we will try to increase that figure in this election,” he said.
He said his eight-year track record as the Bukit Katil assemblyman was also an advantage in his bid to secure a third term.
Adly is facing Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif of PN, Dr Aliza Che Amran (Parti Bersama Malaysia) and Abu Bakar Sabudin (Independent) in a four-cornered contest for the seat.
In the previous state election, Adly retained the seat with a majority of 1,057 votes.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 for polling.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: Heavy rain triggers flash floods in Taman Sri Muda, no displacement reported
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — No evacuations have been carried out in Taman Sri Muda, Section 25 here following flash floods triggered by heavy rain this afternoon, which were also captured in videos circulating on social media.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said a similar incident was also detected in Kampung Baru Hicom, Section 26 during the department’s monitoring around Shah Alam.
“Water has risen at several locations, spilling onto roads due to overflowing drains. However, no evacuations have been carried out in the affected areas. The latest situation shows that the rain has stopped, although the weather remains cloudy,” he said in a statement today.
He said monitoring was also being carried out in other high-risk areas, including Jalan Kebun Bunga in Section 22, Section 13 and Jalan Kebun.
Earlier, social media users shared updates on flash floods following heavy rain between 3 pm and 5 pm today.
The posts included images and videos of areas around Taman Sri Muda and a shopping mall in Bukit Tinggi, Klang, showing rising water levels following the heavy rain. — Bernama

Title: Police secure remand of nine suspects over deadly Sibu brawl
Article:
SIBU, Nov 8 — Nine suspects have been remanded for seven days until Nov 15 to assist in the investigation into the death of a 19-year-old male believed to have been stabbed during a brawl here yesterday.
Sibu District Police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the suspects, aged between 16 and 42, were brought to court at 7.15 am today for the remand application.
He said a post-mortem examination completed today revealed that the victim died of chest injuries.
“The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code,” he said.
The Sibu District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Department launched an operation to track down those believed to be involved after receiving a report at about 2 am yesterday.
All the suspects were rounded up at several locations around Sibu between 10 am and 4 pm yesterday. — Bernama

Title: Second 5G network achieves 90pc coverage ahead of schedule, says Fahmi
Article:
DOHA, Nov 8 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil highlighted Malaysia’s progress in expanding its 5G network at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026, with the country’s second 5G network achieving 90 per cent coverage in October this year, nine months ahead of schedule.
He said the achievement marked significant progress in Malaysia’s transition towards a dual 5G network model aimed at strengthening competition, encouraging investment and improving telecommunications service quality.
Fahmi said Malaysia had also made significant investments in expanding and strengthening its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA) since 2020.
“As of July 2026, approximately 10.12 million premises had been passed by fibre, significantly improving access to high-speed broadband services,” he said at the Digital Leadership Forum Ministerial Panel held in conjunction with MWC Doha 2026 here today.
Fahmi said Malaysia had also made substantial progress in 5G deployment, with the second network achieving 90 per cent coverage nine months ahead of schedule.
He said the development reflected the country’s efforts to establish a competitive and sustainable telecommunications ecosystem while ensuring that consumers benefited from improved service quality.
However, Fahmi stressed that Malaysia’s digital infrastructure development was not solely focused on expanding network coverage, as service quality, affordability and resilience were equally important.
He said these elements must be addressed together to ensure that digital connectivity delivered meaningful benefits to the people.
“Through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, or MCMC, we continue to promote infrastructure sharing and efficient network deployment, while addressing connectivity gaps in underserved communities,” he said.
Fahmi said the Universal Service Provision (USP) framework also played an important role in extending telecommunications services to areas where commercial investment alone might not be viable.
He said the approach enabled Malaysia to balance infrastructure investment with the need to ensure that telecommunications services remained accessible and affordable.
“For Malaysia, a successful network model is one that combines strong infrastructure, sustainable investment, effective regulation and meaningful access for all,” he added.
Fahmi is currently in Doha to lead the Malaysian delegation to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26), which runs from Nov 6 to 11.
His working visit to Doha also carries the important mission of securing Malaysia’s re-election to the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
He is accompanied by Communications Ministry Deputy Secretary-General (Telecommunications Infrastructure) Mano Verabathran.
The Malaysian delegation also comprises representatives from the MCMC and local telecommunications industry players, including Telekom Malaysia (TM), CelcomDigi, Maxis and U Mobile. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia to leverage AI and satellite networks for disaster preparedness
Article:
DOHA, Nov 8 — Malaysia sees significant opportunities to leverage satellite connectivity and artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen disaster preparedness and communications resilience, said Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil.
Speaking at the Digital Leadership Forum Ministerial Panel held in conjunction with Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026 here today, he said emerging technologies could complement conventional telecommunications infrastructure, particularly in remote and disaster-affected areas where alternative connectivity solutions might be required.
He said Malaysia also saw potential in integrating terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks to strengthen communications resilience during emergencies.
“Looking ahead, Malaysia sees opportunities to further leverage emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, satellite connectivity and integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks, to strengthen disaster preparedness and communications resilience.
“These technologies can complement conventional infrastructure, particularly in remote or disaster-affected areas where alternative connectivity solutions may be required,” he said.
Fahmi said Malaysia was placing greater emphasis on strengthening emergency telecommunications capabilities to ensure essential communications remained available when conventional networks were disrupted.
He said reliable connectivity was crucial during disasters as it enabled emergency response teams to coordinate rescue operations and affected communities to access essential information.
“During a disaster, connectivity is not merely a convenience. It can be the difference between receiving timely assistance and being left isolated,” he said.
To address these challenges, Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had developed MCMC PRIME, a mobile radio and internet communications system designed to support connectivity when conventional telecommunications networks are disrupted..
He said the system provided an alternative means of communication during emergencies and supported coordination among response teams while maintaining access to essential information.
He said the initiative was particularly relevant during severe flooding when damaged telecommunications infrastructure or disrupted electricity supply could affect conventional mobile networks.
Fahmi said Malaysia’s approach also emphasised close coordination between MCMC and telecommunications operators, as well as the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) and other relevant authorities.
He said such cooperation was essential to support disaster preparedness and identify affected network infrastructure while coordinating restoration efforts and facilitating communications for emergency responders and affected communities.
He also stressed the importance of timely public warnings and reliable access to official information to enable communities to take appropriate precautionary measures during emergencies.
“Network resilience is not simply about preventing infrastructure failure. It is about ensuring that essential communications can continue, or be restored as quickly as possible, when lives and public safety are at stake,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Nations must decide own digital future, not be dictated to, says Fahmi
Article:
DOHA, Nov 8— Malaysia has called for greater respect for national sovereignty in shaping telecommunications policies, warning against a form of “technology colonialism” in which technologically advanced nations dictate how other countries develop and deploy their digital infrastructure.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said every nation must retain the freedom to determine its own technological direction, particularly as geopolitical rivalries and competing technology ecosystems increasingly influence global telecommunications development.
“There should not be a case of a kind of technology colonialism where if you are the first, then you dictate to others what you should or shouldn’t do, what you can or cannot do.
“Nations are sovereign and should be able to decide their own domestic policy,” he said during a ministerial panel discussion at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026 here today.
Fahmi said Malaysia’s experience in rolling out its 5G network demonstrated the importance of maintaining policy independence while navigating complex geopolitical and diplomatic considerations.
He noted that Malaysia initially adopted a single wholesale network model for its 5G deployment despite recommendations against such an approach by GSMA Intelligence, before subsequently transitioning to a dual-network model.
“Malaysia is unique because we did what GSMA Intelligence said not to do: roll out 5G using a single wholesale network. But we did it anyway, and I was the minister in charge of transitioning it into a dual-network model,” he said.
Fahmi described the transition as a challenging undertaking that required Malaysia to navigate diplomatic sensitivities while balancing domestic priorities against international technological standards.
He stressed that discussions on digital sovereignty should extend beyond technological self-reliance to encompass the broader principle of national sovereignty.
The minister also said an increasingly multipolar global environment demands greater dialogue and engagement among countries to find common ground rather than deepen divisions.
“In this increasingly multipolar age, we need to have more conversations, more engagements, and find meeting points rather than things that split us apart,” he added.
Fahmi said the principle of interoperability, which enables different telecommunications networks and technologies to function together, would face significant tests as countries pursued their respective digital strategies.
He pointed out that ASEAN’s consensus-based approach presents its own unique dynamics, given the absence of a central parliament and the bloc’s strong emphasis on respecting member states’ national sovereignty.
As such, he said, building trust and achieving interoperability requires countries to look beyond their national borders and bolster international cooperation.
Fahmi also highlighted the need to assist emerging nations in bridging digital divides, particularly as the telecommunications sector prepares for quantum migration and quantum-safe communications.
He noted that greater focus should be placed on driving the practical adoption of existing networks before the industry shifts its attention entirely to sixth-generation (6G) technologies.
“Before we talk about 6G, we have to look at who is actually using 5G or 5G-Advanced - that remains a key challenge we are actively addressing in Malaysia,” he said.
Despite the hurdles, Fahmi expressed confidence that international collaboration could spur innovative breakthroughs, particularly from nations not traditionally viewed as global technology leaders.
“There are many challenges, but there are also many opportunities for us to discover solutions together, and sometimes you might find those solutions in the unlikeliest of countries,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Police raid unlicensed KL entertainment outlet, detain 195 underage patrons
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Police detained 195 underage teenagers and a premises manager in a raid on an unlicensed entertainment outlet in the capital after midnight last night.
Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the teenagers detained in the operation, conducted at about 12.30 am, comprised 93 local males, 61 local females, 16 foreign males and 25 foreign females.
He said 16 outlet workers and 219 other patrons were also checked.
He said investigations found that the entertainment outlet was operating without a licence and allowing underage patrons to enter.
“The premises manager is being investigated under Section 29(2) of the Entertainment (Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur) Regulations 1993 for allowing underage patrons into the entertainment premises.
“All those detained, aged between 18 and 64, were taken to the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters for summonses, documentation and further investigation,” he said in a statement today.
Ahmad Azwan said checks found that none of the individuals inspected had any outstanding criminal records, while preliminary urine screening found an adult male patron positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.
He said the operation reflected Kuala Lumpur Police’s commitment to ensuring public safety and well-being.
“Enforcement action will continue to be intensified to curb any illegal activities,” he said.
He also urged members of the public with information on criminal activities to channel it through the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2146 0522 / 03-2146 0585, the Dang Wangi District Police Control Centre at 03-2600 2222 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan candidate for Paya Rumput aims to ease voting process with personalised polling slips
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Paya Rumput state constituency Datuk Azman Abidin has introduced an initiative to help voters check their polling locations and channels ahead of the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14.
Azman, popularly known as Tok Man, said he and his campaign team would assist voters in checking their polling details while campaigning, with the results printed on small slips and handed to them for reference.
He said the initiative used electoral roll data provided by the Election Commission (EC) to candidates, with the information entered into a system specially developed by PH to facilitate the checking and printing of voter slips.
“Under this initiative, campaign workers only need to enter a voter’s identity card number to retrieve information on their polling location, including the school and assigned polling channel,” he told reporters after attending a courtesy visit and meet-and-greet programme with the Paya Rumput state constituency campaign machinery today.
Also present at the programme, held at the PH Main Operations Room in Krubong here, was PKR Advisory Council chairman Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, who is also Bandar Tun Razak Member of Parliament.
Azman, who is also the Prime Minister’s Political Secretary, said the idea for the initiative came about after he found that many voters he met during the campaign period could not remember their respective polling centres and channels.
“With this slip, which is more practical than the standard A4-sized printout used previously, voters can not only check their polling details but also keep it in their wallets or pockets for reference again on polling day,” he said.
On the campaign’s progress as it enters its final week, Azman said he would make full use of the remaining time to reach as many residents of the Paya Rumput constituency as possible.
“We will try to cover all areas and reach out to everyone in Paya Rumput, Insha-Allah. The campaign has been going well, in an orderly and peaceful manner. I hope it will remain so until polling day,” he said.
The 16th Melaka State Election will see a three-cornered contest in Paya Rumput between Azman, Rafie Ahmad of Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar of Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
The EC has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026
. — Bernama

Title: Penang Sentral offers round-the-clock waiting space for travellers, says Zairil
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Nov 8 — Penang Sentral, an integrated transport hub and major commercial development, provides a 24-hour waiting area on Level 1 at its stage bus platform, equipped with basic facilities for passengers.
Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the facility was intended for passengers waiting for buses or their next connecting transport service.
He said Penang Sentral was operated by Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) and not the state government, adding that the waiting area was not meant to serve as accommodation or an overnight stay facility.
“MRCB also explained that public access to the terminal is restricted to Level 1 after 1 am, with visitors not allowed to wait or remain in other areas, including the commercial sections and the Urban Transformation Centre (UTC), which are closed for security and operational reasons,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
He was commenting on a social media post alleging that a passenger had been asked to leave the terminal by security guards after arriving at about 1 am.
The passenger claimed he had been waiting for a ferry to George Town, with his hotel check-in scheduled only for 3 pm the following day.
Feedback from members of the public has also highlighted the need for a dedicated waiting space, particularly for passengers arriving on late-night or early-morning express buses.
University student Hana Nurdira Muhammad Haikal, 20, who studies in Kelantan and frequently returns to Penang during semester breaks, said she often arrived at Penang Sentral early in the morning with her friends, adding that the differing needs of passengers should be taken into consideration.
“I believe MRCB could consider providing a dedicated waiting area for passengers arriving late at night or with early-morning travel schedules. It does not necessarily have to offer accommodation, but should at least have sufficient seating and accessible toilets,” she said.
Kuala Lumpur-based bank officer Shahril Reza Ibrahim, 35, who regularly travels by express bus, said such facilities were important for long-distance passengers, especially those continuing their journeys by ferry.
“MRCB may have its reasons in terms of security and operational control, but from the perspective of user experience, there are still some shortcomings that need to be addressed. As a frequent express bus passenger, I often use Terminal Bersepadu Selatan, which is equipped with a waiting area,” he said.
Penang Sentral serves as an integrated transport hub connecting ferry services, KTM train services, express buses and Rapid Penang buses, with the Mutiara Line LRT also planned to serve the area.
Meanwhile, UTC Seberang Perai, which occupies the third and fourth floors of the terminal and spans more than 60,000 square feet, houses nine government departments, including the Immigration Department and the National Registration Department. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia warns of prolonged rain in four states until Wednesday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of continuous rain at the alert level for several areas in Kelantan, Pahang, Sabah and Terengganu, until Wednesday.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli in Kelantan.
In Pahang, the areas affected are Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin, while the warning covers the whole of Terengganu.
In Sabah, continuous rain is forecast from tomorrow until Wednesday in Kudat and Sandakan, covering Paitan, Telupid, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Kinabatangan.
The public can obtain the latest weather information through MetMalaysia’s official website and social media platforms, as well as its myCuaca mobile application.
For further enquiries, the public can contact the MetMalaysia hotline at 1-300-22-1638. — Bernama

Title: Melaka plans five-year push to transform Kota Laksamana into state capital
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 —Kota Laksamana has the potential to become the new state capital of Melaka due to rapid development that can catalyse economic growth and transform the state's landscape, says Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
He said the state government has formulated a five-year development plan for the area and will work alongside the private sector to realise that potential.
"The plans are in place, but we have yet to integrate them because these concessions were awarded to private companies undertaking projects under the Private Finance Initiative (PFI). This is beyond our control as they have acquired the land.
"However, the state government will coordinate with the private sector, provide necessary support and reduce bureaucracy to accelerate economic activity in Kota Laksamana," he told reporters when met at Jalan Hang Tuah here today.
Ab Rauf said the development plan also encompasses areas under the Straits of Melaka Waterfront Economic Zone (SM-WEZ), covering commercial, residential, healthcare and tourism sectors.
"I appeal to the people to join me in developing Melaka and breathing new life into Kota Laksamana so that it can serve as the new state capital," he said.
Commenting on preparations for the Northeast Monsoon, Ab Rauf said the state government has stepped up disaster preparedness, including identifying 102 flood hotspots across the state.
He said the locations were identified based on records of floods recurring at least three times within three years.
"Preparedness measures include round-the-clock flood monitoring across six major river basins, alongside continuous recording of rainfall data and river water levels.
"The early warning system has also been enhanced with the installation of 14 flood warning sirens and 10 surveillance cameras at strategic locations across Melaka," he added.
Ab Rauf said flood mitigation assets have also been readied, comprising 21 water control gates, 21 pump houses and 14 portable emergency pumps that can be mobilised to critical areas, in addition to monitoring 105 flood retention ponds.
He added that 447 small-scale works worth RM43.8 million have been carried out this year to bolster flood management infrastructure and mitigate disaster risks.
He also advised residents, particularly in coastal areas, to remain vigilant as the high-tide phenomenon expected until Nov 17 could cause flash floods in low-lying areas.
"The state government will continue to issue early alerts and advisories through the Melaka State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) to ensure effective emergency response," he said. — Bernama

Title: BN-Pakatan relationship unaffected by Najib pardon issue, says Zahid
Article:
ISTANBUL, Nov 8 — Differences in political views and positions among parties in the Unity Government have not affected the smooth administration of the government, said Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said the working relationship between BN and Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the government remained good, with the administration of ministries and Cabinet meetings proceeding smoothly and professionally.
“There are no problems in terms of our relationship. We manage the ministries and hold Cabinet meetings every week. Government affairs and administration are carried out professionally, and there have never been any differences of opinion or disputes over the past four years,” he told Malaysian media here at a press conference to wrap up his four-day working visit to Türkiye, which ended today.
Ahmad Zahid was asked to comment on whether the issue of a conditional pardon for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak could affect relations between BN and PH in the Unity Government.
Elaborating,  the Deputy Prime Minister said differences in political approaches and positions among parties should be addressed maturely, particularly when political situations differ at the federal and state levels.
He cited the previous Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections, as well as the ongoing Melaka state election campaign, which highlighted differences in political approaches at the state level despite BN and PH working together in the federal government.
“In my view, political maturity in Malaysia is now at an almost optimum level, and although there are different political moves and approaches, insya-Allah, these will not affect the country’s political stability,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Flood-prone areas under close watch as wet weather looms in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 8 — The Penang Fire and Rescue Department has stepped up patrols and monitoring in flash flood-prone areas throughout the state following forecasts of rain and thunderstorms until Tuesday.
Its director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said the measures were aimed at ensuring that personnel remained at optimal readiness to deal with any possible disasters during the Northeast Monsoon.
“Based on weather forecasts issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), rain and thunderstorms are expected in several areas of Penang from today until Nov 10, with the three-day forecast indicating a relatively frequent rainfall pattern, particularly in the afternoons and evenings,” he told Bernama today.
He said today’s forecast indicated rain in several areas in the morning, followed by thunderstorms in most areas in the afternoon and rain in most places at night.
He said tomorrow’s weather was expected to be wetter, with rain in most areas in the morning and thunderstorms forecast across the state in the afternoon, followed by rain in most places at night.
Mohamad Shoki said that on Tuesday, rain was forecast in several coastal areas in the morning, while conditions were expected to ease slightly in the afternoon and evening, although thunderstorms and rain were still forecast in some areas.
He said that despite the expected wet weather, MetMalaysia had informed that no Level 1 (Alert) Continuous Rain Warning had been issued for Penang so far.
“Following the forecast, the Operations Division of the Penang Fire and Rescue Department advises the public to remain alert to the latest weather warnings issued by the authorities.
“Residents, particularly those living in low-lying and flash flood-prone areas, are urged to avoid travelling along high-risk routes during thunderstorms. Anyone requiring emergency assistance or evacuation is advised to immediately call the 24-hour emergency hotline at 999,” he said, adding that the department was fully prepared to deal with any possible disasters throughout the monsoon period to safeguard lives and public property.
He also shared that monitoring operations involving seven Fire and Rescue Stations on the island and in Seberang Perai, including low-lying settlements and major river basins, began last night and that river levels and water flow at all locations inspected remained under control.
Among the locations monitored in Seberang Perai were Sungai Jawi, Sungai Duri, Sungai Junjong and Sungai Kechil, as well as Kampung Sethu, Kampung Sepulau, Kampung Sanglang and Kampung Valdor, Mohamad Shoki added.
“Monitoring was also conducted at Lahar Yooi, Labuh Banting, Ayer Itam, Jalan Permatang Rawa, Jalan Betik and Jalan Soo Ban Kheang in Bukit Mertajam. On the island, patrols focused on areas around Teluk Kumbar and Balik Pulau, as well as several other hotspots under the supervision of the Lebuh Pantai Fire and Rescue Station,” he said.
He said patrols would continue to enable the Fire and Rescue Department to issue early warnings to residents should there be any sudden changes in water levels. — Bernama

Title: Was a BN convoy given priority? Two-car collision at Melaka traffic lights sparks questions
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — A Threads video is raising questions over whether traffic police gave a Barisan Nasional (BN) convoy priority at the time of a two-car accident at a junction on the Alor Gajah-Melaka Tengah-Jasin (AMJ) highway.
The video from a dashboard camera showed a car turning right at the traffic lights junction while another car was travelling straight when they collided, veering into the front vehicles on a third lane.
The video, posted by Threads user @alfshrf, was shared with claims that traffic police had held back road users to let the convoy through.
On social media, someone remarked that the convoy vehicles carried BN campaign stickers and asked what had earned the group priority on the road.
It noted that the convoy vehicles carried BN campaign stickers, and asked what had earned the group priority on the road.
If the priority was tied to an individual’s security, the post asked who that person was, in what capacity, and whether it extended to the whole convoy.
It said the accident should be investigated, asking whether there had been confusion over instructions and how movement from each direction was controlled.
The post added that video footage alone did not settle who was at fault.
It called on the police to explain how traffic was managed at the time.
It also said questions about the convoy itself should be answered by Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh and the party, since the vehicles carried the identity of the coalition he leads in the state.
Among the questions it asked were who led the convoy, where it was heading, and on what basis other road users were stopped for it.
The post also voiced concern that party convoys appeared to receive treatment ordinary motorists do not, even as campaigning for the state election was still under way.
Malay Mail
could not independently verify the video or the claims accompanying it, and no statement from the police, BN or Ab Rauf was immediately available.

Title: Perak MMEA seizes vessel, probes unauthorised anchoring and reporting lapses
Article:
IPOH, Nov 8 —The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) in Perak detained a cargo vessel suspected of violating the Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952, about 4.3 nautical miles southwest of Pulau Jarak, near Lumut, yesterday.
Its director, Maritime Captain Zainudin Mohd Zuki, said the Lumut Maritime Surveillance System radar detected the Gambian-registered vessel, prompting the Perak Maritime Headquarters Operations Centre to alert enforcement teams for inspection.
He said the vessel had 21 crew members, including 11 Pakistanis, eight Iranians and two Indonesians.
“The vessel was suspected of two offences under the Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952: anchoring without authorisation from the Director of Marine Malaysia and failing to report its arrival in Malaysian waters,” he said in a statement today.
Zainudin said the crew and chief engineer were taken to the Perak Maritime Headquarters to assist in the investigation, while the vessel’s documents were seized for further action. — Bernama

Title: AKPS detains 28-tonne buffalo meat shipment over import document irregularities
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) at Port Klang seized a consignment of buffalo meat, valued at RM413,728 and imported from India, at Port Klang on Friday (Nov 6).
Port Klang AKPS commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said an inspection conducted by enforcement officers at 10.40am detected discrepancies between the halal certificate documents submitted and the information declared in the import permit.
“The documents were found to contain information that did not correspond with the declaration. Following this, the entire consignment weighing 27,984 kilogrammes (kg) was seized for further investigation,” he said in a statement posted on the Port Klang AKPS Facebook page today.
Nik Ezanee said the goods would be handed over to the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS) for further action, with the case being investigated under the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Act 2011 (Act 728).
He also reaffirmed AKPS’ commitment to intensifying enforcement efforts and strengthening controls at the country’s entry points to combat non-compliance, document manipulation and abuse of import procedures. — Bernama

Title: Melaka lacks a real capital, says Ab Rauf, who wants Kota Laksamana to be it
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) wants to turn Kota Laksamana into Melaka’s state capital if it wins the seat in the coming state election, Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said.
He said the idea is part of a plan for a new economic corridor that would reshape the area over the next five years, Berita Harian reported today.
“God willing, I am targeting Kota Laksamana to become the capital of Melaka,” he said at a campaign event at BN’s Kota Laksamana operations room here, attended by MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong and BN candidate Melvin Chua Kew Wei.
He asked who could say where Melaka’s capital is today, then answered that there is none.
“So if we win Kota Laksamana, we will give the people of Kota Laksamana a centre that will become Melaka’s state capital,” he said.
Ab Rauf, who is also acting chief minister, said the corridor would include a medical hub, along with tourism and commercial projects, building on Encore Melaka, Oriental Specialist Hospital and a new shopping centre in Klebang.
He said the work would be done in stages, with the first five years laying the groundwork.
Ab Rauf also said a BN win in Kota Laksamana was not out of reach, expressing confidence that Melvin could spring a surprise.
“Our target is Kota Laksamana, and I think this time, this year, this month, this term, it is not impossible for Melvin to become the assemblyman.
“Time and circumstances call for change, and if we stay where we are, it will be hard to change,” he said.
He said the state government would help provide facilities and cut red tape to speed up development in the area.
Chua faces a three-cornered fight against Pakatan Harapan’s Low Chee Leong of DAP and Parti Bersama Malaysia’s Ethan Lim Zhi Hao.
Low defended the seat in the 2021 election with a majority of 11,494 votes.
Early voting for the 16th Melaka state election is on Tuesday, with polling day this Saturday.

Title: Fake cops cheat retiree of RM179,490 in money laundering scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 —A 73-year-old retiree lost RM179,490 after falling victim to a Macau scam involving fraudsters posing as police officers and accusing him of money laundering and drug trafficking.
Brickfields police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the victim was initially contacted by two unidentified individuals claiming to be police officers, who instructed him to surrender his bank cards, cash and jewellery for investigation purposes.
He said the victim, who panicked, later agreed to meet the suspects at an apartment in Sri Petaling on Sept 8 to hand over the money and valuables as instructed.
“The total losses amounted to RM179,490, involving cash handed over, gold purchases and transfers to three third-party bank accounts,” he said when contacted today.
Hoo said the victim lodged a police report after realising he had been cheated.
Police were checking information with telecommunications companies and reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage to assist investigations under Section 420 of the Penal Code, he added. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for 11 states, federal territories
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are forecast to hit 11 states and all three Federal Territories until 6 pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the adverse weather is expected across the whole of Penang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka, as well as the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Labuan.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, the alert covers Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Kinta, Kampar, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kerian, Selama, Batang Padang and Muallim.
In Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai, Jeli and Gua Musang, while in Pahang, it involves Temerloh, Lipis, Rompin, Bera, Maran, Kuantan, Jerantut and Pekan.
In Johor, the affected areas are Muar, Tangkak and Segamat.
Meanwhile, in Sarawak, bad weather is forecast for Mukah (Dalat, Matu, Daro and Tanjung Manis), Sibu (Sibu), Bintulu (Tatau), Sri Aman (Pantu, Lingga and Sri Aman), Limbang, Miri (Marudi and Bario), Sarikei (Maradong), Kapit (Kapit) and Betong (Pusa and Betong).
In Sabah, the warning covers Kudat, Sandakan (Paitan, Telupid and Tongod), the West Coast, the Interior, and Tawau (Semporna, Tawau, Lahad Datu and Kunak). — Bernama

Title: Melaka first, Bersatu later: Perikatan chairman holds off on disciplinary action
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is putting off any decision on whether to discipline Bersatu until the Melaka state election is out of the way.
PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the coalition had received complaints from its component parties about Bersatu’s conduct, Free Malaysia Today reported.
“We will discuss them at our supreme council meeting.
“We will act based on the facts presented, not on sentiments,” he told reporters after visiting PN’s operations room in Kesidang today.
He did not elaborate on the complaints, saying only that they concerned events before and after the Negeri Sembilan state election in August.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan had earlier said the coalition would act against Bersatu for allegedly breaching its constitution, including by contesting against PN in the Negeri Sembilan polls.
He said charges would be drawn up and Bersatu given enough time to defend itself.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has dismissed the plan as “strange and absurd”, insisting his party broke no rules.
Muhyiddin also noted that Bersatu had reported alleged violations by PAS within PN to the Registrar of Societies (RoS), which had since acted.
The RoS suspended PN in late September and deregistered it on October 20 after Bersatu’s complaint against the coalition’s leadership, before the High Court stayed the deregistration two days later.
PAS cut ties with Bersatu in June, and Muhyiddin later said his party had been sidelined by PN as the PAS-led coalition pursued an alliance with Umno.
The RoS cancelled PN’s registration on October 20 under the Societies Act 1966, but the High Court stayed the decision on October 22 pending a judicial review, allowing PN to contest Melaka.
The RoS and the home minister appealed the next day, with the Court of Appeal due to hear the matter on February 22, 2027.

Title: MB: No dissolution of Negeri Sembilan assembly, Budget sitting to go ahead
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 8 — The Negeri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly will not be allowed to dissolve, and efforts will be made to ensure that its sitting takes place as scheduled, said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
He said all preparations for the tabling of the Negeri Sembilan Budget had been finalised, and the state government was now only waiting for the official date to be set for the sitting.
“Preparations for the Budget are all in place. We have also finalised it and are only waiting for the date to hold the state assembly sitting.
“We will do our best to ensure that it is held as scheduled. There is no question of the state assembly being dissolved. Insya-Allah, as the head of the state government, I will not allow the state assembly to be dissolved,” he told reporters after attending the Deepavali open house hosted by special adviser on Indian community affairs Datuk VS Mogan here today.
He was responding to a question on the state government’s preparations for the upcoming state assembly sitting.
Previously, the state government had planned to begin the next sitting on Nov 26, followed by the tabling of the 2027 State Budget on Nov 27. — Bernama

Title: ‘Mandatory’: Khairy tells Umno and BN voters to back PAS in Bukit Katil
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — Fewer than seven months after Umno formally welcomed him back, Khairy Jamaluddin is on the Melaka campaign trail telling Barisan Nasional (BN) supporters to vote for a PAS candidate.
The former Umno Youth chief said BN voters in Bukit Katil must back the PAS candidate there under the electoral understanding between the two sides, the
New Straits Times
reported today.
“Send word to our friends, for example in Bukit Katil, because there is a PAS candidate there and we did not field a BN candidate,” he was quoted saying at a campaign stop in Duyong.
“Over there, it is mandatory for Umno and BN voters to give their support to PN-PAS,” he added.
PN stands for Perikatan Nasional. The coalition’s legal status has been in doubt since the Registrar of Societies cancelled its registration on October 20 following a complaint by Bersatu, a decision the High Court stayed two days later pending a judicial review that the government is appealing.
Khairy said discipline at the ballot box had to be shown wherever seats had been conceded to partner parties.
Duyong, where PAS is not contesting, was the mirror image, he said, with the Islamist party’s machinery and supporters expected to deliver their votes to BN candidate Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem.
“In areas where PAS is not contesting, such as in Duyong, on behalf of BN and Umno, I am asking for help in the spirit of cooperation and consensus of the Malay-Muslim community, to support our candidate number two, Datuk Helmy, and other candidates from Umno and Barisan Nasional,” he was quoted as saying.
He added that ground readings across Melaka showed joint coordination taking place down to voting district centres and branches, signalling that machinery on the ground was aligned with the seat-sharing strategy.
Khairy was expelled from Umno in January 2023 for breaching party discipline during the 15th general election, and was readmitted unconditionally on April 17 this year under the Gagasan Rumah Bangsa initiative.
Under the Melaka arrangement, BN is fielding 23 candidates, including 18 from Umno, leaving the remaining five of the 28 seats to PAS and its allies, with polling on November 14 and early voting on November 10.

Title: Nearly 3,000 guests, one cake: Anwar joins MIC’s Deepavali celebration in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today attended the Deepavali open house organised by MIC and the Maju Institute of Educational Development (MIED) at Mansion Oncidium Hall in Kota Kemuning here.
He was welcomed by MIC president and MIED chairman Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran, adding to the festive atmosphere at the Festival of Lights celebration, which was attended by nearly 3,000 guests from various ethnic backgrounds.
Anwar spent time mingling with guests and dining with several political leaders, including former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob and MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong.
Commenting on the event, Vigneswaran said the celebration showed that Malaysians could live in harmony and share in the joy of festivals throughout the year.
“This proves that celebrations like this are a clear platform for integration among the races.
“Although there are differences in political backgrounds, events like this can set them aside for the sake of togetherness,” he said.
Vigneswaran also expressed hope that Malaysians would maintain their close ties and make them a strength as the country moved towards comprehensive progress.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim (second from left) with MIC president and Maju Institute of Educational Development (MIED) chairman Tan Sri S.A. Vigneswaran (second from right) at the MIC and MIED Deepavali open house at Mansion Oncidium Hall in Kota Kemuning, Selangor on November 7, 2026. — Bernama pic
Meanwhile, Wee said the event was not only lively but also reflected the unique diversity of Malaysians in a spirit of goodwill.
“This is truly the spirit of goodwill that has long existed among Malaysians, and it must be preserved for the prosperity of our beloved country,” he said.
At the event, Vigneswaran and Wee accompanied Anwar in cutting a cake to mark the highlight of this year’s open house celebration. — Bernama

Title: Small Hindu communities, big Deepavali spirit in Sabah and Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Despite the relatively small Hindu population in Sabah and Sarawak, Deepavali celebrations today brought together people from diverse backgrounds, reflecting a strong spirit of unity.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia estimates that Sarawak has about 5,000 Indians, accounting for 0.2 per cent of its 2.53 million population, while Sabah has around 6,000, or 0.2 per cent of its 3.77 million residents, based on 2026 data.
This year’s celebrations were a different experience for serviceman R. Ruhthiran, 20, as he celebrated the festival away from his family in Klang, Selangor, for the first time.
Stationed in SARAWAK, at Penrissen Camp in Kuching, the second of five siblings said being away from his family was part of the demands of military service.
“I miss my family, but I am enjoying my time here.
“Being separated from loved ones is part of life as a soldier,” he told Bernama before attending prayers at the Sri Maha Mariamman Temple in Batu Lintang.
He said Deepavali celebrations typically began with an early-morning oil bath, followed by wearing new clothes and attending prayers at the temple around 8am.
Going to temples for prayers in the morning is part of the culture and tradition for many Hindus in Malaysia on Deepavali. — Bernama pic
“My mother usually prepares
idli
and
thosai
for breakfast,” he said, adding that the family would return home after prayers before visiting relatives to celebrate together.
Ruhthiran expressed gratitude to his seniors for helping him locate a temple, making it easier to fulfil his religious obligations.
For Kuching resident Pramod Kumar, 67, Deepavali remains a meaningful occasion, though celebrations are more modest because of the state’s relatively small Hindu population.
“We usually start the day with prayers at the temple, followed by a family gathering to celebrate Deepavali and seek blessings,” he said, adding that Kuching celebrates Deepavali much the same way as Peninsular Malaysia and India, but on a smaller scale.
In SABAH, people of various ethnicities and faiths gathered at the Sri Pasupathinath Alayam Temple in Kota Kinabalu to join in the Deepavali festivities.
First-time visitor Geoffrey Lo, 50, said he was excited to experience the Deepavali celebrations at the temple.
“This is my first time here and I am really excited... the food is delicious too,” he said.
Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor is scheduled to attend the 2026 Deepavali gathering at the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) at noon today. — Bernama

Title: Prayers, reunions and open houses: Malaysia welcomes Deepavali
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — A festive mood filled towns and cities across the country as Hindus ushered in Deepavali today with prayers, temple visits, family reunions and gatherings with friends and neighbours.
At the Sri Subramaniar Swamy Temple in Batu Caves near here, the grounds were already buzzing with activity early this morning as families in colourful traditional attire arrived to offer prayers.
A visitor, Vishnu, 36, who came with his wife and two children, said visiting the temple had been a family tradition since his childhood, and one he was now happy to continue with his own family.
He said it was also heartening to see tourists and Malaysians of different races joining in the celebrations.
Meanwhile, in SELANGOR, devotee A. Narmatha, 23, who was met after offering prayers at the Ellai Muniyandi Temple in Setia Alam, hoped this year’s Deepavali would bring happiness and blessings to all Malaysians.
In a Facebook post, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the celebration continued to bring the state’s diverse communities closer together.
He also gave an assurance that the state government would continue to look after the welfare of the Indian community through various initiatives.
In PERAK, about 10,000 Hindus gathered at the Kallumalai Arulmigu Subramaniar Temple at Gunung Cheroh in Ipoh from as early as 6.30 am to offer prayers.
A Hindu woman anoints a girl with blessed ash at the Sri Subramaniya Swami Devasthanam temple along Jalan Kuala Ketil in Sungai Petani, Kedah in conjunction with Deepavali on November 8, 2026. — Bernama pic
Temple chairman R. Seetharaman, 56, said many devotees began the day with prayers at home before heading to the temple, where they arrived in colourful traditional attire carrying offerings of flowers, milk and fruits, before continuing the celebrations with visits to relatives.
In PENANG, the Muniswarar Temple in Jalan Baru and the Arulmigu Karumariamman Temple in Seberang Jaya also drew crowds from early morning, with people of all ages coming together to mark the occasion.
Housewife R. Dewi, 68, from Seberang Jaya, said Deepavali was a wonderful opportunity to strengthen family ties and catch up with neighbours of other races, while passing the spirit of unity on to the younger generation.
In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the Sri Bala Thandayuthapani Temple in Seremban held two prayer sessions, one in the morning and another set for later in the afternoon, to give devotees more space and comfort while avoiding overcrowding.
In KEDAH, this year’s celebrations brought extra joy and relief to Hindus in Anak Bukit who had been affected by floods previously.
Resident R. Nandran, 43, said he was grateful to be able to celebrate peacefully with his family without worrying about his home being flooded as it had been last year.
His family was also hosting an open house, with halal dishes such as mutton curry, thosai and briyani prepared for their Malay and Chinese friends and neighbours.
Hindu devotees visiting the Arulmigu Karumariamman temple in Butterworth, Penang to perform prayers in conjunction with Deepavali on November 8, 2026. — Bernama pic
For S. Khulanasari, 36, who lives in Penang, the celebration was made even more special by her return to Kuala Kedah to spend Deepavali with her parents after work commitments had kept her away for two years.
In KELANTAN, the Indian community in Kampung Ladang Kerrila, Tanah Merah, kept the celebrations simple but meaningful, starting the day with prayers at the Sri Maha Mariamman Temple.
Resident G. Maran, 45, said the occasion was a chance to reunite with relatives who had returned to their hometowns and enjoy traditional treats.
In JOHOR, the 115-year-old Arulmigu Rajamariamman Devasthanam Temple in Johor Bahru welcomed about 2,500 Hindu devotees, including foreign workers from India and Nepal.
Temple treasurer Murali Sami said the historic temple also drew foreign tourists, particularly from Western countries and China, who were keen to admire its architecture and experience Hindu traditions.
Hindu devotees posing for family photos at the Kallumalai Arulmigu Subramaniar temple at Gunung Cheroh in Ipoh, Perak while performing prayers in conjunction with Deepavali on November 8, 2026. — Bernama pic
In PAHANG, the home of R. Palamal, 65, in Kuantan was filled with laughter and family cheer as more than 30 relatives from different parts of the country gathered to celebrate after offering prayers at the Sri Mariamman Temple.
In PERLIS, the Arulmigu Arumugaswamy Dhevasthanam Temple in Kangar was already welcoming devotees from 7 am, with the celebrations drawing the local Indian community together.
Temple chairman Datuk Dr R. Hari Ram said more than 200 devotees were expected to visit the temple.
The temple management had also prepared and distributed food to residents of an old folks’ home, spreading the joy of the Festival of Lights beyond the temple grounds. — Bernama

Title: Wheel off, bumper wrecked: Chery says collision, not faulty parts to blame for viral NKVE car damage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Chery Auto Malaysia has moved to head off online speculation after images of a damaged Chery Tiggo Cross with a detached wheel and its axle spread on social media.
The incident happened when the Chery car collided with a Perodua Myvi on the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) yesterday.
“We wish to clarify that the damage to the front bumper and detachment of the wheel were a result of the accident and not due to a failure of the vehicle’s component parts,” Chery said in a statement.
It said its team had already contacted the customer involved and was providing the necessary assistance.
The company urged the public to refrain from sharing unverified information, warning that it could cause unnecessary concern among road users and contribute to misinformation.
It added that the safety and well-being of its customers remained its utmost priority, and directed those with enquiries to the Chery Careline at 03-9388 0888.
Pictures of the scene on social media showed both vehicles damaged in the right lane of the highway.
Chery’s statement did not detail how the crash happened or whether investigations by the authorities had been completed.
The incident comes about a month after the Road Transport Department temporarily suspended the vehicle type approval certificate for the Chery Omoda 5 following a separate incident in Johor Bahru.
In that case last month, the rear axle assembly of an Omoda 5 was reported to have come loose, prompting the department to launch a technical investigation and an audit of the production process, assembly and component suppliers.
Chery later announced a recall campaign for certain Omoda 5 variants, offering free inspection and replacement of the related parts.

Title: Heavy rain, strong winds expected in Johor, Melaka and parts of three other states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Several areas in five states are forecast to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 3 pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
MetMalaysia said in a statement that the adverse weather was expected to affect the whole of Johor and Melaka.
In Sabah, the affected areas are the West Coast and Interior, covering Keningau, Pensiangan, Tambunan and Sook; Kudat; Sandakan (Paitan, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan, Tongod and Telupid); and Tawau (Kalabakan and Tawau).
Similar weather conditions are also forecast in several areas in Pahang, namely Temerloh, Pulau Tioman, Bera and Rompin, as well as in Negeri Sembilan, covering Jempol, Tampin, Seremban, Rembau and Kuala Pilah districts. — Bernama

Title: Ceilings leak at Seberang Jaya Hospital, no patients affected (VIDEO)
Article:
SEBERANG PERAI, Nov 8 — Healthcare workers were seen holding umbrellas indoors at Seberang Jaya Hospital last night as rainwater poured through leaking ceilings and spread across flooded corridors, in video footage that has since gone viral.
Penang Health director Dr Zulhizzam Abdullah confirmed that heavy rain and strong winds sent water seeping into several parts of the hospital, the
New Straits Times
reported today.
“Most affected areas involved the hospital’s older building blocks, though several newer buildings were also impacted,” he was quoted as saying.
“This was an unforeseen incident due to torrential rain, gale-force winds and massive runoff.
“However, no patients were affected, and no adverse incidents were reported,” he added.
https://www.facebook.com/bernamaofficial/videos/butterworth-hujan-lebat-luar-biasa-berserta-angin-kencang-mengakibatkan-beberapa/1923907435685920/
Dr Zulhizzam said the hospital’s engineering and maintenance management department had moved to address the situation immediately.
Malaysia is currently in the north-east monsoon season, which is expected to continue until March next year.

Title: Health Ministry investigating claims of illness after consuming Gardenia products
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 8 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is awaiting laboratory analysis results and will conduct follow-up inspections at the Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd factory to verify compliance with the Food Act 1983 following complaints of alleged food poisoning involving the company’s products.
In a statement today, MOH said preliminary investigations were underway into complaints circulating on social media and media reports of alleged food poisoning after consumption of Gardenia products, particularly Gardenia Original Classic White Bread and Twiggies Choc-A-Lot.
“MOH has sought an explanation from Gardenia Bakeries (KL). According to the company, its internal investigation found no deviations in production processes, recipe changes or non-compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) and food safety controls for the products concerned.
“Traceability of the products involved remains limited as the batch numbers and expiry dates provided were incomplete. However, the remaining products and their packaging were collected with the complainants’ consent for laboratory analysis,” MOH said.
MOH stressed that the company’s findings were based on its internal investigation and could not yet be used as the basis for a definitive conclusion on the cause of the symptoms reported.
The ministry also assured that appropriate enforcement action would be taken if evidence of legal violations or risks to food safety were found.
Meanwhile, MOH advised the public against making speculation that could cause confusion, while individuals experiencing symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhoea or discomfort after consuming the suspected products were urged to seek medical attention immediately and report the matter to the nearest District Health Office.
Food safety complaints can be channelled through the Public Complaints Management System (SiSPAA) at
https://moh.spab.gov.my/
or the Food Safety and Quality Programme’s Facebook page.
Recently, a Threads user claimed to have suffered food poisoning after consuming two Gardenia products, sparking public attention and discussion on social media over their safety. — Bernama

Title: Melaka Polls: Adly calls for transparency on BN's manifesto promises
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) must provide detailed evidence to support its claim that it had fulfilled 97 per cent of the promises in its manifesto for the 15th Melaka State Election in 2021, said Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari.
He called on Melaka BN to provide a comprehensive list of its achievements for the people to assess the actual implementation status of the 103 initiatives outlined in the manifesto across five main thrusts.
“The claimed achievements should be accompanied by a complete list showing the status and commitments so that voters can make their own assessment,” he said at PH’s daily press conference at the coalition’s main operations room in Bukit Baru here today.
Adly, who is defending the Bukit Katil seat in the 16th Melaka State Election, said transparency in presenting manifesto achievements was important to ensure that every commitment announced by the government could be assessed based on actual implementation outcomes, rather than merely percentage figures.
He also said that based on a summary of the Auditor-General’s Report, the Melaka government suffered a deficit in 2024, with revenue of RM490 million against expenditure of RM519 million.
He said the figures underscored the importance of prudent financial management, as well as ensuring that every spending decision was properly documented and produced verifiable results.
“Sometimes we may be able to increase revenue, but expenditure management must also be given priority… that is why, according to the 2024 records, the (state government’s) revenue was RM490 million, while expenditure stood at RM519 million,” he said.
According to Adly, Melaka recorded a financial surplus of RM50 million in 2019 when he led the state administration.
He said PH, through its “Melaka Rumah Kita” aspirations, was offering clean, transparent and integrity-driven governance, including ensuring that every ringgit of public funds was managed prudently.
He said voters were entitled to clear information on the state government’s achievements so that they could make informed assessments ahead of the state election.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
— Bernama
